header: Date: 2026-11-02 | Time: 14:00 UTC | Duration: 45m | Attendees: Maya Chen, Ethan Park (Redwood); Priya Nair, Liam O'Connor, Samantha Ruiz (BlueWave Analytics)
summary: Redwood AE/SE ran a migration demo focused on parity mapping from OpenAI/Anthropic/Together stacks to the Redwood API. Discussed API parameter mapping, streaming & function call parity, embeddings differences, performance expectations, security (VPC/KMS/SOC2), and next steps for a short benchmark pilot and security deep dive.
topics: Security: VPC, KMS, SOC2, audit logs
transcript:
[00:00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya, AE at Redwood. Ethan from our SE team is here, and we're excited to walk through migration options from OpenAI/Anthropic/Together to Redwood.
[00:00:10] Priya: Hi Maya, thanks. I'm Priya, CTO at BlueWave. Liam and Samantha here with me. We run a mix of chat, embedding search, and a re-ranking pipeline.
[00:00:22] Ethan: Great, quick agenda: high-level parity mapping, live demo of the API and Console, short bit on Optimize recommendations, then Q&A and next steps.
[00:00:35] Liam: Sounds good. Our main concerns are behavior parity (we need same outputs), latency/cost, and security for PII.
[00:00:44] Maya: Understood. We'll start with parameter mapping. Redwood's text generation endpoint accepts temperature, top_p, max_tokens similar names but small differences in default handling.
[00:00:58] Ethan: Right, for OpenAI folks, temperature and top_p map 1:1. For Anthropic there are different system prompt conventions — we provide a compatibility layer and recommend canonicalizing system messages before calling. Together models have slightly different tokenization; our SDK handles tokenization normalization so prompt lengths map predictably.
[00:01:18] Samantha: Tokenization normalization sounds useful, we had subtle token-count differences moving between vendors.
[00:01:25] Ethan: Yeah, we log tokenization deltas in Console so you can see where the counts shift.
[00:01:32] Priya: What about function calling? We rely heavily on structured outputs.
[00:01:37] Maya: Redwood supports function/tool calling parity — same pattern: declare schema, Redwood will return matched function call objects. Note: there may be small differences in field ordering or error semantically when model abstains; we have mapping docs.
[00:01:51] Ethan: Also streaming: we stream tokens in the same chunked way. One quirk: if you're used to OpenAI's chunk boundaries, Redwood emits partial JSON tokens slightly differently because of our kernel-level batching, which can cause small JSON fragments mid-stream — we provide SDK helpers to rebuild messages robustly.
[00:02:10] Liam: So we won't see breakage in our clients? We rely on streaming for low latency.
[00:02:15] Ethan: No breakage; SDK handles it. If you use raw HTTP stream you might need a small parser tweak.
[00:02:22] Priya: Embeddings — we currently use OpenAI/Anthropic embeddings for semantic search. How similar are Redwood embeddings?
[00:02:29] Maya: Redwood offers curated open models and can run the same checkpoints where license permits. Embedding vectors are model-dependent; we provide scripts to map dimensions and normalization. For semantic parity, we recommend re-indexing and running a small offline comparison. That's part of the pilot.
[00:02:46] Samantha: Any on-the-fly conversion to avoid full reindex?
[00:02:49] Ethan: We can do delta-updates and reweighting but full reindex for accuracy is recommended. We'll help with tooling.
[00:02:56] Priya: Cost and latency — give us an expectation versus OpenAI and Anthropic.
[00:03:01] Ethan: It varies by model and quantization. For many workloads Redwood matches Anthropic/OpenAI at similar latency but with better cost via batching and KV cache. On dedicated pools you'll see more consistent p95 latency.
[00:03:15] Liam: Any numbers? p50/p95?
[00:03:18] Ethan: In our benchmarks, p50 for chat ~120ms token stepping for 8k context on A100-class backends, p95 around 350-450ms depending on sequence length and batching. For hosted instances on our shared plane numbers can be slightly higher under burst. We'll share the benchmark sheet.
[00:03:36] Priya: We need deterministic tail latency; that's why we asked about Dedicated.
[00:03:40] Maya: Dedicated reserved capacity gives SLAs and predictable throughput; autoscaling policies can be tuned.
[00:03:47] Samantha: Security questions: we need VPC, SSO, KMS, and audit logs — can you confirm?
[00:03:53] Maya: Yes: Redwood Private supports VPC peering and customer-managed networking. We integrate with KMS/HSM for key wrapping, SSO/SAML for identity, RBAC, and immutable audit logs. We're SOC2 and SOC2 Type II reports are available in our trust center.
[00:04:08] Priya: Any difference when moving from OpenAI hosted to your Private on-prem?
[00:04:13] Ethan: On Private you control network egress and key material; the API remains the same, just a different endpoint and auth. There are some ops differences for kernel tuning and autoscaler config but functionally parity is high.
[00:04:27] Liam: Let's see a short live demo?
[00:04:30] Maya: Sure — Ethan will demo.
[00:04:34] [screen share start] Ethan: I'll run three snippets: a chat call, a function call, and an embedding. First chat: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.sh/v1/chat with body {"model":"redwood-chat-8k","messages":[{"role":"system","content":"You are..."},{"role":"user","content":"Summarize sales call"}], "temperature":0.2} — returns streamed tokens.
[00:05:00] [00:05:00] Liam: Looks familiar, where's the schema for system role mapping?
[00:05:04] Ethan: In our parity doc; system role is normalized to prompt + system metadata.
[00:05:09] [00:05:12] Ethan: Next function call example: declare functions with JSON schema, Redwood will route back a function call payload — here's a live snippet. Notice the call id and stop reason fields differ slightly from OpenAI naming (we use 'stop_code' vs 'finish_reason' in some models).
[00:05:28] Priya: Noted — we'll adapt parser.
[00:05:31] Ethan: Embedding example: POST /v1/embeddings with model redwood-embed-1024, get back vector of 1024 floats. We return metadata with tokenizer delta so you can audit token differences.
[00:05:45] Samantha: Do you support batching of embeddings in a single call?
[00:05:48] Ethan: Yes, and Optimize will suggest batch sizes based on model and your typical sequence length to minimize GPU memory overhead.
[00:05:56] Priya: About the Console: can we see token-level cost and per-route dashboards?
[00:06:01] Maya: Yes — Console shows per-route model usage, token breakdown, latency histograms, and attribution to accounts. You can set alerts for quality regressions tied to evals.
[00:06:11] Liam: For migration parity mapping, what do you provide as artifacts?
[00:06:15] Maya: We'll provide a parity spreadsheet mapping endpoints, params, response fields, suggested parser diffs, SDK snippets across OpenAI/Anthropic/Together -> Redwood. Also a benchmark template that runs identical prompts across each provider and records tokens, latency, and quality metrics.
[00:06:30] Priya: That parity spreadsheet is critical.
[00:06:33] Maya: Action item noted.
[00:06:36] [pause / background noise]
[00:07:00] Liam: A random question — Together models sometimes have different special token behavior causing subtle rerank changes. Any knobs?
[00:07:07] Ethan: You can control stop tokens and post-process with our normalization layer. If rerank changes appear, we suggest temperature 0 for deterministic scoring and compare logit scores when available.
[00:07:20] Samantha: Governance: how long do you retain logs and transcripts?
[00:07:24] Maya: Default retention is 90 days for hosted, but for Dedicated/Private you control retention via policy, and we can configure long-term storage or forward logs to your S3/compliance bucket. Audit trails are retained per enterprise contract.
[00:07:37] Priya: Excellent. For the pilot, we need a data handling addendum?
[00:07:42] Maya: We can attach a DPA and SOC2 artifacts; Ethan will follow up with the security contacts.
[00:07:48] Ethan: I'll schedule a security deep dive — we usually cover VPC peering steps, IAM roles, KMS flow diagrams, and any compliance checklist you need.
[00:07:58] Priya: How quick is onboarding? We have a target to begin a pilot by mid November.
[00:08:04] Maya: That's feasible. For a minimal pilot we provision a sandbox Dedicated or Private test tenant, share SDK keys, and run your benchmark over 48 hours. Typical turnaround 3-5 business days for sandbox provisioning.
[00:08:17] Liam: For rerank pipeline we'll want to test end-to-end latency with our microservice calls. Can Redwood instrument traces?
[00:08:24] Ethan: Yes, we emit tracing metadata and you can ingest into Jaeger or our Console. We also provide per-request trace ids to correlate logs.
[00:08:33] Samantha: Any gotchas on the network side? We use strict egress policies.
[00:08:37] Ethan: For Private, you can either peer or run in-hosted VPC; if peering ensure routes and NAT rules allow model nodes to pull dependencies during initialization. We'll provide a network checklist.
[00:08:49] [00:08:55] Priya: Pricing — can you ballpark pilot pricing for 50k tokens/day?
[00:08:59] Maya: For hosted API it's usage-based; we can provide exact numbers after model selection. For Dedicated pilot there is a small reserved capacity fee plus usage. I'll send a draft pricing sheet.
[00:09:12] Liam: Are there built-in A/B tools to compare models or rollbacks?
[00:09:16] Maya: Yes, Console supports canary rollouts and A/B with automatic fallback. You can route a percent of traffic to Redwood while keeping production on OpenAI and fall back if latency degrades.
[00:09:27] Priya: That would let us test in prod safely.
[00:09:30] Ethan: Quick note on Optimize: it will recommend quantization profiles and batching settings. For some models quantized FP16/INT8 profiles reduce cost significantly with minimal quality drop; we'll surface expected delta.
[00:09:43] Priya: We will need a quality regression test set — we'll provide.
[00:09:46] Maya: Perfect.
[00:09:48] [cross-talk] Liam: Are hallucination guards available?
[00:09:51] Ethan: You can use retrieval augmentation and include source attribution, and our Eval hooks can detect hallucination patterns on your prompt set.
[00:09:59] Priya: OK I think this covers most of it; let's go through action items.
[00:10:03] Maya: Recap: we will share parity mapping spreadsheet, kick off 48h benchmark, schedule security deep dive, and send pricing.
[00:10:12] Priya: Sounds good. Liam or Sam — any other asks?
[00:10:16] Liam: Please include sample code for streaming parser adjustments.
[00:10:19] Samantha: And the VPC networking checklist.
[00:10:22] Maya: Noted.
[00:10:25] [00:10:30] Ethan: I'll take the benchmarks and streaming snippets. Maya will send parity sheet and pricing.
[00:10:36] Priya: Great thanks, looking forward to the pilot.
[00:10:40] Maya: Thanks all, we'll follow up.
[00:10:44] [meeting end — informal chatter]
